2. Load data for the remaining validation genomes (rice, maize, dm6, danio)

Only the divergence/integrity columns are needed for the correlation analysis below, so these loading chunks skip the superfamily relabelling used for tair10’s distribution plots.

3. Analysis 1: correlation between identity and integrity — real vs. mode-2 simulated

For each of the five validation genomes, compute the Pearson and Spearman correlation between TE loci divergence (1 - identity) and integrity, separately for (a) the real/original genome (empirical, from RepeatMasker output) and (b) the mode-2 simulated digital replica. Loci with missing or out-of-range (itg < 0) integrity values are excluded, consistent with the filtering already used for the distribution plots above.

4. Analysis 2: mode-1 correlation baseline (“by construction ~0”)

Modes 0 and 1 both draw identity and integrity from independent distributions (Gaussian identity, Beta integrity) at simulation time, so any identity-integrity correlation observed under either mode is not designed in - it is the null baseline against which the real/mode-2 correlations in Analysis 1 should be judged. This section uses mode 1 only: the TEgenomeSimulator_tair10_ch1_m0_* runs originally considered for the mode-0 baseline turned out to have been simulated using a TE mutagenesis table (TElib_sim_list_mode2.table) generated by mode 2, not mode 0’s own independent draw, so they are not a valid mode-0 baseline and are excluded. Since a genuine mode-0 run uses the same underlying identity/integrity sampling model as mode 1, mode 1’s result is representative of both. Data reused from the item 29 replicate-run work (no new simulation):

5. Analysis 3: non-independence caveat and family-level robustness check

TE loci within a genome are not independent observations: loci belonging to the same TE family share evolutionary history (a single ancestral insertion event, correlated copy number and age), so the per-locus cor.test() results in Analyses 1-2 above have an effective sample size well below the raw n_loci reported - the same non-independence issue already raised for the Shannon-entropy/Wilcoxon analysis elsewhere in this revision (overlapping/non-independent windows inflating apparent significance). Non-independence inflates the p-value’s apparent confidence, not the correlation coefficient itself, so the effect size and its confidence interval - not the p-value - should be treated as the primary evidence from Analyses 1-2.

As a robustness check, each TE family is collapsed to its median divergence and median integrity (one data point per family, regardless of how many loci it contains), and the same Pearson/Spearman test is re-run on those family-level medians, real vs. mode-2, across all 5 species. If the family-level result agrees in sign and rough magnitude with the per-locus result, that is evidence the per-locus correlation is not solely a within-family pseudoreplication artefact.

Family-level robustness check: Pearson/Spearman correlation between median divergence and median integrity per TE family (one point per family, addressing within-family pseudoreplication), real vs. mode-2 simulated.
